item.description: Emily Wilson, who has translated bothThe OdysseyandThe Iliad, joins Thomas Jones to talk through Christopher Nolan’s film adaptation. As Wilson argues, while Homer’sOdysseymight seem the perfect source material for Nolan, the ancient Greek poem excels at many things the director isn’t so good at, not least dialogue and characterisation.

item.description: Albert Camus’s short life began in Algiers in 1913 and ended in a car crash near Paris in 1960. item.description: How do we give old words new voices? What must a translator lose – and what might she gain – when she moves between languages, bringing ancient stories to modern life? Emily Wilson has spent a lifetime wrestling with these questions. Here, she invites us to consider the meaning and messages of translators from antiquity to today – and offers fresh insights into her own work on Homer.
